salesCopy.tagline: Your Notes Are Plain Files. Let Them Work For You.
salesCopy.secondaryTagline: The **FREE** 62-page guide to Obsidian automation, from your first template to AI agents running on your vault
salesCopy.problem: Most guides to Obsidian automation are lists of plugins. Install this, install that. What they never explain is how the pieces fit together, in what order to adopt them, and where it all leads. So people bolt automation onto a vault that has no clear structure, and the automation reproduces the mess, faster.
problemPoints: The same manual steps every day: creating notes, filling frontmatter, moving files
Notes that drift out of shape because nothing keeps them consistent
A dozen plugins installed, no idea which ones actually matter
Scripts and templates that break as soon as the vault grows
No clear picture of where AI fits without handing your notes to a chatbot
Automating too early, then maintaining a machine you don't understand
salesCopy.agitate: The cost compounds. Every hour spent on manual filing is an hour not spent thinking. Every inconsistent note makes queries less trustworthy. And when AI agents finally arrive on your vault, they inherit whatever mess is there. Without a mental model, you keep adding tools instead of building a system.
agitatePoints: Hours lost every week to work a template could have done
Dataview queries you stop trusting because the data underneath is inconsistent
Plugin sprawl that slows the app down and nobody can explain
Backups and sync that were never automated, until the day they were needed
AI experiments that fail because the vault was never made machine-readable
Restarting the vault from scratch, again
salesCopy.solution: This **FREE** guide gives you the complete map. Obsidian automation is three layers stacked on one idea: your notes are plain files, so anything can operate on them. Layer 1 inside Obsidian, Layer 2 around the vault, Layer 3 AI agents on top. The guide covers every plugin and technique that matters, in the order to adopt them, with the safety practices that keep the system trustworthy.
solutionPoints: **A mental model** that tells you what to automate first, and what to leave alone
**Seven jobs** Layer 1 plugins should do for you, with the plugins that do them
**Layer 2 and 3 in depth**: Git, CLI, REST and MCP, scheduled jobs, AI agents, hooks, skills
**A real production setup**: how a 20,000+ note vault runs with an AI assistant inside it

originStory.title: Why This Guide Exists
originStory.subtitle: From one vault, 20,000+ notes, and a lot of broken scripts
originStory.story:
I automated my vault the wrong way first: plugins before structure, scripts before note types. It worked until it did not. The version that lasted started from a simple idea: notes are plain files, so anything can operate on them, as long as the files are consistent.

This guide is the map I wish I had at the start, including the parts about what not to automate.

methodology.title: The Three Layers
methodology.subtitle: One idea, three places to apply it

steps.title: Layer 3: AI agents on the vault

steps.title: The adoption path

methodology.philosophy: Automation is what keeps a knowledge system trustworthy. It is not a collection of plugins.
